channel.title: Smart Cities Dive - Article Feed
channel.description: Latest articles from Smart Cities Dive (smartcitiesdive.com)

item.title: Environmental groups are suing the EPA for gutting a key climate rule. Cities and states vow to do the same.
item.description: California will challenge EPA’s “endangerment finding” repeal in court. The U.S. Conference of Mayors pledges to "fight for policy that addresses climate change with the seriousness that it requires."

item.title: Oregon mandates heat pumps in new housing
item.description: The update to the state’s residential energy code could save residents of housing built after the change an average of $125 a month in energy costs, an analysis found.

item.title: HUD rule would bar families with mixed immigration status from federally funded housing
item.description: The proposed policy changes would result in the eviction of tens of thousands of tenants from agency-supported housing, nonprofit groups say.

item.title: States sue Energy Department for terminating $8B in clean energy funding
item.description: The Trump administration unlawfully bypassed Congress and made politically motivated cuts to programs created through the IRA and IIJA, the lawsuit claims.

item.title: Pritzker proposes statewide zoning standards to boost housing in Illinois
item.description: Illinois Gov. JB Pritzker targeted local housing regulations in his State of the State this week, unveiling a path for more “missing middle” development.

item.title: Pedestrian, biking infrastructure improvements on tap for Atlanta suburb
item.description: Sandy Springs, Georgia, residents want trails and green space, they told the city. With funds from a local sales tax, two projects are underway.

item.title: The business case for dash cams: prioritizing ROI in a precarious fiscal climate
item.description: How city fleets are protecting drivers and budgets.

item.title: How a skills-first hiring strategy transforms organizational performance for local governments
item.description: The public sector can set a standard showing that capability matters more than pedigree and economic opportunity should be based on what a person can do, not just whether they have a college degree.

item.title: 3 state-level parking reform efforts to watch
item.description: To encourage housing development, more states are ending parking spot minimums.

item.title: California lends $590M to keep Bay Area transit running
item.description: The loan will prevent service cuts in the near term, but a long-term solution depends on a November 2026 regional ballot measure.
